issues.legal_issue: A debtor may be barred by waiver and estoppel from challenging a secured creditor’s enforcement procedure after conduct that induced the creditor to delay enforcement and third-party rights arose.
material_facts: After receiving enforcement notices, the borrower repeatedly sought restructuring and additional time instead of objecting to the enforcement measures.
The borrower made assurances about payments, additional investment, and supporting documents, but did not fulfil them.
The bank deferred enforcement while considering the borrower’s proposals and granted further opportunities to regularise the account.
The borrower did not challenge successive auction attempts or the final auction notice, and challenged the enforcement only after the property had been sold and third-party rights had arisen.
issues.conclusion: The borrower had waived and was estopped from challenging the alleged failure to respond to its representation; the Court therefore decided this issue in favour of the bank without determining whether the statutory response requirement had been breached.
issues.legal_principle: Section 13(3A) of the SARFAESI Act requires consideration of a borrower’s representation, but a statutory right created for an individual’s benefit may be waived, including by implied conduct, unless waiver is prohibited or contrary to public policy. Waiver requires knowledge of the right and conduct showing its intentional abandonment; estoppel may prevent a party from taking an inconsistent position after inducing reliance. The Court applied ITC Ltd. v. Blue Coast Hotels Ltd. and the principles discussed in Commissioner of Customs v. Virgo Steels, AL.AR. Vellayan Chettiar v. Government of the Province of Madras, S. Raghbir Singh Gill v. S. Gurcharan Singh Tohra, Krishan Lal v. State of J&K, Martin & Harris Ltd. v. VIth Additional District Judge, Bank of India v. O.P. Swarnakar, Shri Lachoo Mal v. Shri Radhey Shyam, and Pravesh Kumar Sachdeva v. State of Uttar Pradesh. The Court also noted that relief is discretionary and may be withheld or moulded where the circumstances, including intervening third-party interests, make it inequitable.

rule.if: sarfaesi_enforcement_challenge and repeated_restructuring_requests and unfulfilled_repayment_assurances and creditor_indulgence_and_delay and failure_to_contest_measures_when_taken and challenge_after_third_party_rights_created

predicates.sarfaesi_enforcement_challenge: The proceeding challenges a secured creditor’s enforcement of a secured asset.
predicates.repeated_restructuring_requests: The debtor repeatedly asked the creditor to restructure the debt or defer enforcement.
predicates.unfulfilled_repayment_assurances: The debtor made assurances about repayment, investment, or supporting steps and did not fulfil them.
predicates.creditor_indulgence_and_delay: The creditor granted the debtor time or other indulgence and delayed enforcement while considering the debtor’s proposals.
predicates.failure_to_contest_measures_when_taken: The debtor did not object to or challenge enforcement measures when they were taken.
predicates.challenge_after_third_party_rights_creat: The debtor challenged the enforcement after the asset had been transferred and third-party rights had arisen.

issues.definition: When an enforcement challenge follows repeated unfulfilled proposals, creditor indulgence and delay, silence as measures are taken, and a challenge only after third-party rights arise, the debtor is barred from challenging the procedure by waiver and estoppel.

issues.legal_issue: A secured creditor is not required to sell machinery separately from the land and building when enforcing its security merely because the machinery has been valued separately.
material_facts: The valuation report separately valued the land, building, and machinery, identifying numerous individual machinery items.
The borrower did not dispute or challenge the valuation report.
The machinery was sold together with the land and building, and the confirmed auction price exceeded the fair market valuation of the combined property.
The borrower did not establish prejudice or loss from the combined sale.
issues.conclusion: The machinery did not have to be separately auctioned or sold, and the High Court’s contrary finding was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: Under the SARFAESI enforcement framework, the secured creditor may sell the mortgaged property in a manner directed toward securing the best value for recovery of the debt. Separate valuation of machinery does not itself require separate sale; the Court noted that prejudice was not established and that the confirmed price exceeded the fair market valuation. The Court relied on no earlier case for this issue.

rule.if: secured_asset_auction_challenge and machinery_valued_separately and valuation_report_unchallenged and no_prejudice_established and combined_sale_price_exceeded_fair_market_value

predicates.secured_asset_auction_challenge: The proceeding challenges the sale of a secured asset by auction.
predicates.machinery_valued_separately: The valuation assessed the machinery separately from the land and building.
predicates.valuation_report_unchallenged: The debtor did not dispute or challenge the valuation report.
predicates.no_prejudice_established: The debtor did not establish that selling the machinery with the land and building caused prejudice or loss.
predicates.combined_sale_price_exceeded_fair_market: The price obtained for the combined sale exceeded the fair market value of the land, building, and machinery.

issues.definition: If a secured-asset auction challenge concerns separately valued machinery sold with the land and building, and the valuation is unchallenged, prejudice is unproved, and the combined price exceeds fair market value, the machinery need not be sold separately.

issues.legal_issue: A valuation report’s age does not by itself invalidate an auction where earlier auctions failed, the reserve price was reduced, and the eventual bid exceeded both the reserve price and the assessed fair market value.
material_facts: The valuation report preceded the auction in question.
Earlier attempts to auction the property attracted no bidders.
The creditor reduced the reserve price before the later auction.
The successful bid exceeded both the reduced reserve price and the fair market value stated in the valuation report.
issues.conclusion: The date of the valuation report did not provide a basis to invalidate the sale or require a fresh valuation in the circumstances of the case.
issues.legal_principle: The Court assessed the valuation issue in light of the failed earlier auctions, the reduced reserve price, and the successful bid’s relationship to both the reserve price and the report’s fair market value. It relied on no earlier case or specific statutory provision for this issue.

rule.if: secured_asset_auction_challenge and valuation_report_predated_auction and earlier_auctions_failed and reserve_price_was_reduced and successful_bid_exceeded_reserve_and_fair_market_value

predicates.secured_asset_auction_challenge: The proceeding challenges the sale of a secured asset by auction.
predicates.valuation_report_predated_auction: The valuation report was prepared before the auction being challenged.
predicates.earlier_auctions_failed: Earlier attempts to auction the asset did not produce a successful bidder.
predicates.reserve_price_was_reduced: The creditor reduced the reserve price before a later auction.
predicates.successful_bid_exceeded_reserve_and_fair: The successful bid exceeded both the applicable reserve price and the fair market value stated in the valuation report.

issues.definition: When earlier auctions fail, the reserve price is reduced, and the later successful bid exceeds both that reserve and the assessed fair market value, the report’s earlier date alone does not invalidate the sale.
